priceSnapshot.note: Price is 81,264.9, up 6.32 percent on the 24-hour open of 76,433.6 and 485.8 points above the midday handover at 80,779.1. The day closes as the largest single-session advance in this file. The decisive new fact arrived after the US cash close: Farside now shows 18 September US spot Bitcoin ETF flows at PLUS 322.3 million USD. Midday could only say that number was pending; it has printed, it is the first flow reading to price the breakout, and it is the largest positive day since the series turned. That is the institutional confirmation this desk said it was waiting for, and it removes the main objection to the move. The second confirmation is leverage: open interest on the BTC-USDT perp is 2,477,822,670 USD against 2,428,535,885 at midday, another 49.3 million and 2.03 percent of fresh commitment while price rose. Both legs of the breakout are now funded rather than squeezed. Against that stands a specific, measurable failure. Midday published an add gate at 81,267.0 requiring a SETTLED 1H close. Over the six hours since, price tagged or exceeded that level on FOUR separate hourly bars - highs of 81,407.0, 81,374.9, 81,304.3 and 81,267.0 - and closed under it every single time. The closest attempt settled 81,242.2 at 21:00 UTC, short by 24.8 points. The last settled hour closed 80,903.0. A market that touches a level four times in six hours and cannot close through it is not accumulating for the next leg, it is distributing into supply. That refusal, and not the price, is what sets tonight's stance.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below 80,568.6, RAISED 1,501.4 points from the 80,070.0 that midday published and never came close to testing. 80,568.6 is the low of the current OKX daily bucket, which opened at 16:00 UTC, and it sits 195.6 points under the 80,764.2 evening low and 334.4 points under the 80,903.0 lowest settled hourly close. It is 696.3 points under the mark, 1.47 times the 472.96-point 1H ATR - wider than the 1.2-to-1.3 multiple this file normally runs, and deliberately so, because a weekend tape produces wicks that a weekday tape does not and a stop that is too tight through Saturday is a donation. The settled-close requirement is unchanged and is the rule that refused four bad adds tonight.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above 81,267.0, UNCHANGED from midday. This is the disciplined call and it is worth being explicit about why the level does not move. The file's own 17 September lesson is that a trigger which has been PAID FOR is no longer a trigger. This one was not paid for: it was tagged four times on price and refused four times on the close, the best attempt falling 24.8 points short. An unfired gate is not stale, it is simply unmet, and moving it up to 81,407.0 because price wicked there would be rewarding a touch this desk has explicitly decided not to trade. The gate stays exactly where it was until the market either settles through it or breaks the shelf beneath.

decisionBox.changed: The direction did not change; the exposure did. Bias stays BULLISH and the tilt stays bullish, probabilities move from 56/28/16 to 57/27/16 and confidence from 6.75 to 6.90 - the upgrade paid for entirely by the 322.3 million USD ETF print and the further 2.03 percent build in open interest. Position moves from ADD to TAKE_PROFIT. That is not a contradiction of the bias, it is a weekend decision: the structural case is stronger than it was at midday and the tactical entry is worse, because the add gate has now been refused four times and the 1H RSI is still 75.08. The reduce gate is raised 1,501.4 points to 80,568.6, the floor of the evening shelf. The add gate is held at 81,267.0 precisely because it never fired. The 77,167.3 invalidation is untouched for a third consecutive session. The one genuinely new instruction is the resting stop: stopOrder goes to RECOMMENDED for the first time this week, at 80,568.6, because the next report is roughly thirty hours away across a weekend and a resting order is the only protection that survives a gap.

overnightRisk: The gap to the next report is the widest of the week and it spans a weekend. This is the last scheduled run until roughly 02:00 COT Saturday, and the sessions after that sit inside the thinnest liquidity of the crypto week, when the same order flow moves price further and stop cascades run unopposed. Four specific things could matter. First and most likely, a failed-breakout unwind: price has been refused at 81,267.0 four times and the whole 6.32 percent advance was built in about thirty-six hours, so there is no volume shelf between 80,568.6 and the 80,070.1 post-squeeze floor, and below that the CoinGlass forward map is close to empty until roughly 77,500 and then a heavy band near 76,000. A weekend flush through 80,568.6 has very little structural bid under it until 79,250.0. Second, the leverage build cuts both ways: open interest has risen 6.6 percent across today's two readings to 2.478 billion USD, so the positioning that funded the breakout is also fuel for a liquidation cascade if the shelf breaks, and tonight's realized tape is already 25 to 1 short-dominated, meaning the shorts who would have cushioned a fall have largely been flushed out. Third, rates: the US 10-year settled at 5.00 percent, up 5.3 basis points on the day, and it has been the most reliable macro headwind in this file all month; a further move above 5.05 percent in Sunday's futures reopen would pressure every long-duration asset including this one. Fourth, and the only one that is genuinely unknowable, headline risk - no US ETF flow data prints again until Monday evening, so the bid that confirmed this move today is simply absent from Saturday and Sunday, and the market will trade two full days without it. The resting stop at 80,568.6 is set for exactly this reason: it is the only instruction in this report that works while nobody is watching.

liquidation.note: 875,965 USD across 76 fills and overwhelmingly one-sided - 864,385 USD of SHORT liquidations against 11,580 USD of longs. This is by far the heaviest bucket on the tape in the 19:47:17 to 00:31:38 UTC window and it is effectively AT the money, its centre sitting 14.9 points under spot. The reading is specific: the market has spent the evening re-establishing shorts into the 81,250 shelf and having them force-covered, four times over, without ever managing to settle an hour above 81,267.0. Shorts are being paid out at this level and price still cannot clear it, which means the covering is being absorbed by real supply rather than igniting a continuation.

The brightest band on the CoinGlass forward heatmap immediately above spot, read off the right-hand price axis at roughly 81,500 and extending across the full width of the 48-hour window. This is projected resting leverage, not realized fills, so the USD magnitude is qualitative - but the level is solid and it is the first real pocket of fuel above the 81,407.0 high. If the add gate ever settles, this is what the move is reaching for.

50,091 USD across 20 fills, 49,516 short against 574 long. This was the heaviest cluster on the midday tape at 1,376,396 USD and it has now thinned by a factor of twenty-seven. The fuel here has been genuinely consumed rather than refilled, which is why the 81,000 level no longer pulls the way it did six hours ago.

24,311 USD across only 4 fills and 100 percent LONG liquidations - the sole long-side cluster anywhere on tonight's tape. It marks the 80,764.2 evening low almost exactly, which is the point: the one time price probed the bottom of the evening shelf it found and cleared a thin pocket of long leverage, and there was not much there. That thinness is an argument for the shelf holding and an argument for the air pocket beneath it being real, at the same time.

A distinct band on the CoinGlass forward heatmap just under the evening shelf, read at roughly 80,350 off the price axis. It sits between the 80,568.6 reduce level and the 80,070.1 post-squeeze floor, which is the zone a weekend flush would have to cut through. Qualitative magnitude, solid level.

A teal band on the forward heatmap around 77,500, the first meaningful structure below the 79,250.0 shelf. Between 80,070.1 and here the forward map is close to empty, which is the honest definition of an air pocket: the breakout traversed this ground in about thirty-six hours and left no resting leverage behind it.

The heaviest band on the downside of the forward heatmap, a bright green-to-yellow streak at roughly 76,000 that corresponds to the pre-breakout consolidation and the 76,349.4 low of the last 24 hours. This is where a genuine failed-breakout unwind would be drawn. It is 5,264.9 points away and nothing in tonight's data argues it is in play this weekend - it is recorded because the endday report is the one that has to name the tail.

liquidityMagnet.note: Pull is UP, but it is a weaker and more ambiguous up than midday's. The weight argument is overwhelming on its face - 913,901 USD of short liquidations against 36,465 USD of longs over four hours and forty-four minutes, a 25.1-to-1 tilt, against midday's 5.9-to-1 - and on a normal read that says the market keeps paying out shorts and should keep grinding higher. The qualification is the one that matters tonight: almost all of that weight, 875,965 of 913,901 USD, sits in a single bucket at 81,250 that is AT the money rather than above it, and price has been unable to settle an hour above 81,267.0 through four attempts while that fuel burned. Short liquidations that do not produce a settled breakout are supply being absorbed, not demand being unleashed. The nearest genuine magnet ABOVE is the forward band at roughly 81,500, 235.1 points away; the nearest below is the at-the-money 81,250 cluster. So the pull is up and the follow-through is not there, which is precisely the configuration that argues for banking a slice rather than pressing.

On the same verified series the 4H ATR14 is 961.52 (1.18 percent), the 1H ATR14 is 472.96 (0.58 percent) and the 15m ATR14 is 186.58 (0.23 percent). That is a market whose range is compressing at the highs after a vertical day, which resolves as either a coiled continuation or a failed breakout and does not tell you which.

scalpContext.intradayBias: Bullish structure pinned under a hard ceiling. The evening box is 80,764.2 to 81,407.0 and the operative level inside it is 81,267.0, which has been tagged and refused on four separate hourly closes. With the 15m RSI reset to 57.01 and the 15m ATR down 40 percent to 186.58, the range is compressing - the middle of this box is the worst place to initiate in either direction, and the weekend tape makes every false break more expensive than usual.

etfFlows.note: The number midday was waiting for has printed and it is decisive: 18 September US spot Bitcoin ETF flows are PLUS 322.3 million USD, the largest positive day in the recent series and the first reading to price the breakout. It follows 17 September at plus 159.5 million, so the streak is two positive days and the institutional bid turned the day BEFORE the range broke rather than chasing it afterwards. The five-session net is now minus 104.6 million against minus 720.7 million at the midday read - a 616.1 million USD improvement in one print, which is how completely this single day reshapes the flow picture. The sequencing is the whole story: minus 450.4 on the 15th, minus 295.9 on the 16th, then plus 159.5 and plus 322.3. Source: Farside Investors, Bitcoin ETF Flow all-data table, read in-browser at 19:38 COT. No further flow data prints until Monday evening, so the weekend trades without this bid.

liquidations.note: Three readings, and unlike midday they do not all say the same thing. First, open interest is 2,477,822,670 USD against 2,428,535,885 at the 12:46 COT midday read - up 49.3 million and 2.03 percent, on top of the 4.50 percent it added this morning, so roughly 6.6 percent of fresh commitment has been layered on across today's two readings. New capital is still being committed; this remains a funded move, not a squeeze. Second, realized liquidations over the 19:47:17 to 00:31:38 UTC window are 913,901 USD of shorts against 36,465 USD of longs, a 25.1-to-1 skew that is far more lopsided than midday's 5.9-to-1 - but 875,965 USD of it sits in one at-the-money bucket at 81,250 that produced four refused breakout attempts rather than a breakout, which makes it absorbed supply rather than unleashed demand. Third, the skew field carries the OKX long-short ACCOUNT ratio at 0.99, down from 1.01 at midday and 1.54 this morning. Retail accounts are now fractionally NET SHORT into a 6.32 percent up day - contrarian-supportive, and it means there is still no crowded long to flush. Funding is 0.01000 percent, the exact neutral baseline, with a negative premium of minus 0.0001957, so there is no leverage tax on this move in either direction. For cross-reference the CoinGlass all-exchange aggregate reads 147.37 billion USD of open interest (up 9.40 percent), 634.9 million USD of 24-hour liquidations (up 212.38 percent) and a 24-hour long/short split of 51.66 to 48.34.

indices.note: Settled close 18 September at 721.45, up 0.63 percent, on 48.3 million shares - the heaviest volume of the 21-day window and a fresh high for the period. Two strong sessions back to back after the 1.73 percent jump on the 17th, and the fund now sits at the very top of its monthly band. That is a risk-on tape and it is the correct macro backdrop for what BTC did today, but it also means there is no cheapness here for a monthly DCA: the 100th percentile reading is literal, the close IS the 21-day high. RSI 58.16 shows the strength is not yet overextended in momentum terms, so this is 'rich, not dangerous' - a scheduled contribution is fine, an oversized one is not.

divergences.note: A clean regular bearish divergence and the first one this file has recorded during the breakout. At the 12:46 COT midday read the session high was 81,267.0 with the 1H RSI at 84.54. Price subsequently printed a HIGHER high of 81,407.0 - the peak came in the 19:00 UTC hour, around 14:00 COT - while the 1H RSI fell to 75.08 by this 19:35 COT read. That is 140.0 points more price on 9.46 fewer RSI points, so momentum did not confirm the new high. This is not a reversal signal on its own and it sits inside a frame whose MACD histogram is still positive, but it is the mechanical companion to the four refused settled closes at 81,267.0 and it is the specific reason tonight's report banks a slice rather than pressing the position into a weekend.

calibration.rollingRecord: 100 of 198 directional tilts correct — 50.51 percent lifetime.
calibration.note: Midday got both halves right and this is the first session in several where that can be said without qualification. The directional call: midday published BULLISH at 56 bull against 16 bear with price at 80,779.1, and price is 81,264.9 - 485.8 points and 0.60 percent higher. Correct in sign, lifting the lifetime line to 100 of 198. The 80,070.0 reduce gate did NOT fire and was never approached: the lowest trade of the window was 80,764.2, leaving 694.2 points of clearance, and the lowest settled hourly close was 80,903.0 at 833.0 points clear. The 77,167.3 invalidation held with 4,097.6 points of clearance, its widest margin yet. The 81,267.0 add gate did NOT fire, and the manner of the failure is the most instructive data point of the day: price tagged or exceeded the level on FOUR separate hourly bars - 81,407.0 at 19:00 UTC, 81,374.9 at 22:00, 81,304.3 at 21:00 and 81,267.0 at 16:00 - and closed beneath it every time, the best attempt settling 81,242.2 and missing by 24.8 points. The settled-close rule therefore refused four adds in six hours. On a pure price basis every one of those touches looked like a breakout; on a close basis none of them was. That is the rule earning its keep for the seventh and eighth time in this file, and it is why the gate is being held at 81,267.0 rather than raised. Discretionary: midday BOUGHT a 15.00 USDT spot tranche at 80,779.1 against an explicit warning that the 1H RSI was 84.54, and spot marks 81,264.9, so the tranche is 485.8 points onside, roughly plus 0.090 USDT on a 15.00 USDT slice. Hence acting_helped TRUE. The deliberate undersizing also looks correct in hindsight rather than merely cautious: a full re-entry at 80,779.1 would have bought the day's distribution zone, and the 47.78 USDT of dry powder it preserved is what gives this session and tomorrow's midnight run something to work with. The open question carried forward is the one the four refusals raise - whether 81,267.0 is a pause inside a trend or the ceiling of the move - and no data available tonight resolves it.
